summary: James Wilson Bright was a linguist who studied at Lafayette College and Johns Hopkins University. He taught at Cornell University in 1885 and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins from 1905 to 1925.

Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Tekchok Dorje, Gyurme Thutop Namgyal, and Tai Situ Pema Nyinje Wangpo, and also taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Jamie Hubbard is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Kazuo Okabe and earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He held endowed professorships at Smith College, attested in 2016 and 2026.

Jampa Lhundup is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. Attested in 2026, he studied as an Assistant Professor of Art History and served on the faculty at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Jampa Losang Panglung was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He obtained his Geshe Lharamapa at Sera Monastery and his Magister and doctorate at the University of Munich, later working at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and Jamgon Kongtrul Rinpoche.

Jampa Samten is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, serving as Director (attested 2015) and later as a re-employed Professor (attested 2026).

Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen (1912–1947) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Kalu Rinpoche, Chatral Sangye Dorje, Tsennyi Tulku Jampal Norbu, and the 13th Dalai Lama, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama.

Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö (1893–1959) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under teachers including Khenpo Thupten, Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and succeeded Dzongsar Khyentse Jamyang Chokyi Wangpo.

Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (1820–1892) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Rigdzin Zangpo, Gyurme Sangye Kunga, and Shechen Gyurme Thutob Namgyal, among others, while also teaching Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé.
Jamyang Sherab Chokyi Nangwa studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Jan Baudouin de Courtenay was a linguist who studied at Warsaw, Charles, Berlin, and Leipzig universities. He held posts at Kazan, Dorpat, Jagiellonian University, Saint Petersburg, Warsaw, and the John Paul II Catholic University of Lublin.

Jan Chozen Bays is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada. She served as a teacher at the Zen Community of Oregon from 1985 and as abbess of Great Vow Zen Monastery around 2002.

Jan Christian Schaffert works in Indology and computational studies. Attested in 2026, he studied and worked as a collaborator on the EdiKILex project at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Jan Dolensky is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, attested in 2013, under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Jan Fontein was a scholar of Asian art and sinology who earned his PhD at Leiden University. He held curatorial posts at the Museum of Asian Art and Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, and was a visiting scholar at Royal Ontario Museum.
Jan Gonda was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Utrecht and Leiden universities. He held the Chair of Sanskrit (1929) and taught Indology (1932–1976) at Utrecht University.

Jan Jakob Maria de Groot was a sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University. He served as a professor at Leiden University (1891–1912) and as Professor of Sinology at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1912–1921).
Jan Jaworski was a scholar of sinology, japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Warsaw under Stanisław Schayer and Jean Przyluski.

Jan N. Bremmer is a religious studies and history scholar who studied at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and the University of Bristol. He taught at Utrecht University (1974–1990) and held a professorship at the University of Groningen (1990–2005).
